What a /21 means

A /21 holds 2,048 addresses. Blocks this size are usually site or data-centre allocations that get divided into smaller subnets.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /21 uses 21 network bits and leaves 11 host bits, so the block contains 2,048 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−21) − 2 = 2,048 − 2 = 2,046.

Configuration examples

Cisco IOS

interface Vlan10
 ip address 172.16.0.1 255.255.248.0
!
access-list 10 permit 172.16.0.0 0.0.7.255

Juniper Junos

set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 172.16.0.1/21

Linux

ip addr add 172.16.0.1/21 dev eth0

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /21?

2,046. A /21 has 2,048 addresses; the first is the network address and the last is the broadcast address, so 2,046 are usable.

What is the subnet mask for /21?

255.255.248.0. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 0.0.7.255.
